title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products

tasks.short: Answer customer questions about technical products, prices, availability and credit terms.

steps.what: Clarify the customer's question and intended application during a call.
Find relevant specifications, limitations and warranty clauses in the {DOCS}.
Check account prices, stock and existing credit terms in the {ERP}.
Resolve uncertain application fit with a sales engineer.
Approve requested credit exceptions against the credit policy.
Write and send the customer answer through the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Clarified question, current commercial facts and approved technical references.
loop.output: Answer draft with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Match prices and terms exactly to records; require sources for technical claims and representative approval.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing, conflicting or stale facts route to a person.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard facts, but varied application questions need short explanations grounded in supplied references.

steps.what: Record the answer and promised follow-up in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A staff answer desk joins approved references in the {DOCS} with account-specific facts from the {ERP}. A bounded loop drafts sourced answers for approval before the {EMAIL} sends them, while the {WORKFLOW} records the exchange in the {CRM} and routes exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical documents and live commercial records sit apart. Account pricing, document versions and exception ownership need explicit controls.
tasks.enabler_now: Search, record lookups and templates already exist. AI coding can reduce the effort of connecting them; a bounded loop can turn checked facts into a readable draft.
tasks.still_hard: Application ambiguity, stale manuals and stock changes remain. Credit concessions and unsupported technical claims require accountable judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise what the customer is really asking and when a technically correct answer would still mislead.

ambition.what: Offer smaller distributor accounts a staffed technical question service.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time searching and copying, and more time resolving application questions. Existing credit and technical approval rights stay unchanged.

reach.task: Triage application questions before detailed engineering review.
reach.learn: Operating limits, failure modes and the evidence required for an engineering escalation.

evidence.claim: Record lookups and approved document retrieval can support routine sales answers without autonomous agents.
The digest reports a chatbot fare-answer liability case; applying that concern to technical sales answers is an inference.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: This describes a mid-size European technical seller with telephone clarification and written follow-up.
Shares average routine questions and occasional technical or credit escalations; not every case follows every branch.
The initial scope is one product family and one commercial entity.
GDPR requires appropriate access and retention controls. EU AI Act duties depend on deployment; any customer-facing AI interface needs applicable disclosure.
Access estimates include applicable employee consultation under national rules. Seller monitoring would need separate assessment; the Netherlands has the consent requirement identified in [S13].
Build ranges are working effort and exclude unpredictable procurement or consultation waiting periods.
unknowns: Available interfaces and permissions for the {ERP}, {CRM} and {DOCS}.
Coverage, ownership and version quality of technical manuals.
Frequency of credit exceptions and unclear applications.
Countries of operation and existing employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Can document search reliably distinguish product variants and superseded manuals?
Which freshness checks are needed before stock or price information is sent?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed implementation?
new_work: Review answer drafts and unresolved questions.
Maintain document versions, source ownership and access rules.
Investigate stale records, failed lookups and incorrect answers.
tasks.statement: Answer customers' questions about products, prices, availability, or credit terms.

tasks.short: Prepare and issue quotes with prices, credit terms and technical bid specifications.

steps.what: Read the request and identify requirements from the {EMAIL} and attachments.

loop.input: Quote request, attachments and recorded customer requirements.
loop.output: Structured quote requirements with source passages and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate units, quantities, item identifiers and required fields; representative confirms ambiguous requirements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; conflicting or incomplete requirements return to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests contain varied free text and attachment layouts. Structured requests bypass the loop.

steps.what: Select compatible items and options in the {ERP} quotation screen.
Apply account prices, standard discounts and existing terms in the {ERP}.
Approve discounts or commercial terms outside delegated limits.
Assemble the quote and bid specifications using templates in the {DOCS}.
Check the completed quote and send it through the {EMAIL}.
Re-enter issued quote details and validity dates in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: A bounded extractor converts unstructured requests into reviewed requirements, then deterministic rules check compatibility and generate quote documents from the {ERP} and {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes commercial exceptions, requires approval before sending, and writes the issued quote directly to the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product rules and technical clauses were scattered, while quote documents and commercial records needed manual reconciliation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration, pricing and template generation are established methods. AI coding can reduce implementation effort, with a small extraction loop handling unstructured requests.
tasks.still_hard: Encoding product compatibility and maintaining exceptional clauses can cost more than building the generator. Novel applications and contractual deviations still need specialists.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a compliant configuration meets the customer's actual purpose and whether a concession is commercially justified.

ambition.what: Provide a comparison of compliant alternatives with each complex quote.

tasks.altitude: The representative spends more time discussing options and less time assembling documents. Recommendations can include checked alternatives; discount and credit authority remain explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Prepare compliant technical alternatives for a bid.
reach.learn: Compatibility rules, specification interpretation and when an alternative requires engineering approval.

reach.task: Convert an accepted quote into an order without rekeying.
reach.learn: Item identifiers, revision control and order validation requirements.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad offers product configuration linked to ERP and CRM, with human checking described in the digest.
The ZARGES vendor case reports quote preparation falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds; this is not a forecast for this design.
Rule-based pricing and approved clause assembly need no model; unfamiliar request formats can use bounded extraction.

assumptions: Today, the {ERP} supports quotation records, while bid documents and the {CRM} still require separate work.
Approval time is averaged across a mix of routine quotes and commercial exceptions.
The pilot covers one product family with maintained price lists and approved technical clauses.
Credit exceptions retain finance approval; the sales manager cannot override that authority.
GDPR governs customer and contact data. The proposed quote workflow does not make consumer financing decisions.
Access and applicable consultation under national rules are included in the access range; elapsed waiting time may be longer.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates.
unknowns: Current quotation capabilities and integration rights in the {ERP}.
Whether product rules exist in a maintainable form.
Approval thresholds, quote volumes and exception frequency.
Ownership of technical clauses, translations and commercial templates.
research_questions: Can existing quotation configuration cover compatibility rules before custom code is needed?
Which bid requirements resist reliable structured extraction?
How should rule and template versions be retained to reproduce an issued quote?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and final quotes.
Maintain compatibility rules, prices, clauses and approval limits.
Test changes against representative configurations and exception cases.
Resolve failed document generation and record synchronisation.
tasks.statement: Quote prices, credit terms, or other bid specifications.

tasks.short: Explain relevant product features and limitations using customer needs and technical knowledge.

steps.what: Review the customer's requirements and application context in the {CRM}.
Find relevant capabilities, operating limits and supporting evidence in the {DOCS}.
Assess which features matter and identify unresolved application risks.
Validate uncertain performance or compatibility claims with a sales engineer.
Prepare a customer-specific feature comparison and explanation in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Reviewed feature assessment, approved technical evidence and customer application context.
loop.output: Feature-to-need explanation with limitations, conditions and source references.
loop.check: Compare numbers and units exactly; require sources for claims and retain all material limitations.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported claims are omitted and flagged for human handling.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables can compare specifications, but explaining their relevance to varied applications needs contextual writing.

steps.what: Explain relevant features, demonstrate use and discuss limitations with the customer.
Record confirmed fit, limitations and unresolved questions in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: The {CRM} presents confirmed application requirements, while the {DOCS} provides approved specifications and limitations. A bounded loop drafts an explanation from the representative's assessment, with specialist approval for uncertain claims and a structured {CRM} form for recording the final recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the right revision and translating specifications into customer relevance took time. Generic presentations did not preserve application-specific caveats.
tasks.enabler_now: Document search and structured comparison are established capabilities. AI coding can connect them cheaply, and bounded drafting can adapt reviewed evidence into customer language.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete site conditions and interactions between products can invalidate a plausible recommendation. Explaining uncertainty and verifying understanding remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Connect a feature to the customer's operating reality, explain trade-offs honestly and recognise when the evidence does not support a recommendation.

ambition.what: Provide an application limits briefing before a technical purchase.

tasks.altitude: The representative arrives with clearer evidence and spends more time discussing trade-offs. They can recommend better-scoped alternatives, while engineering retains authority over unresolved technical claims.

reach.task: Assess application suitability before a formal engineering study.
reach.learn: Operating envelopes, measurement uncertainty and the boundary between sales advice and engineering validation.

reach.task: Design a demonstration around a customer's operating constraints.
reach.learn: How to test understanding and show limitations as clearly as benefits.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad demonstrates commercial availability of product configuration; this does not establish autonomous suitability judgement.
Approved document retrieval, structured comparison and bounded drafting can support technical explanations.
Application judgement and customer understanding remain human responsibilities; remaining effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: Requirements from discovery are available, but may still need clarification before a recommendation.
Technical escalation time is averaged across cases; routine explanations do not always need a sales engineer.
The demonstration step describes a remote discussion; physical demonstrations use the same evidence and judgement boundaries.
Structured recording reuses the approved explanation and recommendation fields; new observations are entered by the representative.
The pilot covers one product family and uses approved documentation rather than generating new performance claims.
GDPR applies to customer records. The EU AI Act and any sector-specific duties must be assessed for the actual deployment.
Access estimates include applicable employee consultation under national rules; no call analytics or employee scoring is assumed.
unknowns: Product safety implications and sector-specific approval requirements.
Completeness and revision quality of technical evidence.
The boundary between representative advice and mandatory engineering validation.
Whether the {CRM} already supports structured recommendation records.
research_questions: Can evidence retrieval reliably preserve variant-specific limits and test conditions?
Does generated wording retain all material qualifications across supported languages?
Which applications require formal engineering validation rather than sales guidance?
new_work: Review generated explanations and source references.
Maintain product revisions, limitations and escalation criteria.
Correct misleading comparisons and capture newly discovered application constraints.
Keep recommendation records aligned with the advice actually given.
tasks.statement: Emphasize product features, based on analyses of customers' needs and on technical knowledge of product capabilities and limitations.

tasks.short: Negotiate prices, delivery commitments and other sales terms with technical buyers.

steps.what: Review account history, quoted products, costs and current delivery constraints.
Calculate discount options, margin effects and permitted concessions.
Discuss trade-offs and negotiate provisional terms with the buyer.
Record provisional terms and explain any requested exceptions.
Approve exceptions beyond the representative's delegated commercial limits.
Send the approved terms to the buyer and update the opportunity.

tasks.design: A calculator combines account data from the {CRM}, costs and availability from the {ERP}, and approved concession rules. A structured form in the {CRM} routes exceptional terms through the {WORKFLOW}; approved terms produce a confirmation in the {EMAIL} after the representative checks it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost, delivery and delegation data were separated. Maintaining the calculator and approval links took more effort than using a workbook.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing interfaces and faster AI-assisted coding reduce the effort of connecting records and implementing explicit concession rules.
tasks.still_hard: Buyer priorities, technical risk and bargaining power remain contextual. Delivery estimates and costs can change during negotiations.
tasks.human_edge: The representative reads hesitation, protects trust and trades concessions against commitments the buyer actually values.

ambition.what: Live margin checks for each proposed concession during negotiations

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to assembling facts and recalculating offers. The representative can evaluate concessions during the conversation within existing delegation limits; approval rights do not expand.

reach.task: Review a proposed discount against margin and account value.
reach.learn: Contribution margin, concession sequencing and commercial delegation.

reach.task: Assess whether a delivery or performance promise is technically supportable.
reach.learn: Application limits, implementation dependencies and technical escalation.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad links product configuration and quoting to ERP and CRM records.
Explicit price, margin and delegation rules can generate concession options without a model.
Negotiation usually retains substantial human conversation despite faster preparation.

assumptions: The company sells mainly to organisational buyers and maintains approved commercial delegation limits.
The time split covers preparation, conversation and paperwork; exception approval time is averaged across cases.
Terms within delegated limits bypass sales manager approval.
The proposed preparation and paperwork changes do not require an autonomous agent.
Build ranges assume one product family and existing interfaces. GDPR applies to buyer contact data.
unknowns: Whether current costs and credible delivery estimates are accessible.
Which concessions require commercial, finance or legal approval.
How often representatives use a workbook for concession calculations.
Whether the existing {CRM} supports structured terms and approvals.
research_questions: Which concession combinations can be expressed as explicit rules?
How stale can costs and availability be before a negotiation brief becomes misleading?
Do proposed activity logs require employee consultation under national rules?
new_work: Maintain price, margin and delegation rules.
Resolve stale or conflicting cost and delivery inputs.
Check generated confirmations before sending.
Review exceptional concessions and maintain integration access.
tasks.statement: Negotiate prices or terms of sales or service agreements.

tasks.short: Keep customer contacts, account details and sales activity records accurate in the customer system.

steps.what: Open the customer account and gather verified account changes and completed sales activities.
Check account identifiers, addresses and commercial fields against the finance customer master.
Enter validated details and link completed activities to the correct account.
Resolve duplicate contacts, ambiguous account links and conflicting details.
Request missing contact or account details from the customer.

tasks.design: Configured rules in the {CRM} collect structured updates and link completed sales activities, while an integration compares shared account fields with the {ERP}. Validated updates write automatically, conflicts enter a review queue, and an approved template in the {EMAIL} requests essential missing details through a form in the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Shared fields lacked clear ownership and consistent identifiers. Representatives compensated by comparing screens and entering the same information again.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record rules cover most updates. Faster integration development makes field ownership, validation and reliable synchronisation affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Subsidiaries, shared contacts and disputed account ownership create ambiguous matches. GDPR retention and access requirements must fit actual customer data use.
tasks.human_edge: The representative recognises relationship context and knows when apparently similar records represent different buyers or buying centres.

ambition.what: An account handover pack showing verified contacts, open commitments and unresolved data gaps

tasks.altitude: Routine account maintenance largely leaves the representative's week, leaving a small conflict queue and more customer-facing time. Account correction authority stays within existing permissions; finance-controlled fields remain with the finance team.

reach.task: Validate a new customer's identity and required account fields.
reach.learn: Entity identifiers, account hierarchies and required onboarding evidence.

reach.task: Resolve mismatched delivery and billing account details before order processing.
reach.learn: Customer master ownership, address validation and downstream order effects.

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-10; 10-30 if new employee monitoring requires consultation under national rules

evidence.claim: Structured customer record maintenance is commonly handled by configured record rules and integrations.
Explicit field ownership and stable account identifiers allow deterministic synchronisation without a model.
Ambiguous account merges need human judgement because errors can affect several downstream records.

assumptions: Most updates arrive as structured, verified data, consistent with the supplied prior.
Free-text account changes are redirected to a structured form or handled as exceptions.
The {ERP} owns finance-controlled customer fields; the {CRM} owns sales relationship fields.
Automatic external requests use approved factual templates, permitted recipients and frequency limits.
No new employee performance scoring is included. Build ranges cover one customer master connection.
unknowns: Which system owns each shared field.
Whether stable customer identifiers exist across the {CRM} and {ERP}.
The duplicate rate and proportion of changes arriving only in free text.
Applicable retention periods, access permissions and employee consultation arrangements.
Whether current activity capture would expand employee monitoring.
research_questions: Which native {CRM} rules already remove manual entry?
What match criteria safely distinguish legal entities, sites and buying centres?
Which changes require finance approval rather than a sales correction?
What consultation is required under applicable national rules before rollout?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous matches and approve account merges.
Maintain field ownership, validation and synchronisation rules.
Handle failed updates and bounced detail requests.
Review retention, access and deletion propagation.
Check that activity capture remains within its approved purpose.
tasks.statement: Maintain customer records, using automated systems.

tasks.short: Exchange sales tactics and market information with colleagues and agree useful follow-up actions.

steps.what: Gather recent account outcomes, pipeline changes and sales results.
Review market notes and prepare examples worth discussing.

loop.input: Access-approved sales evidence pack, market notes and prospect notes.
loop.output: Discussion brief with sourced examples, conflicting observations and open questions.
loop.check: Link every factual claim to its source, verify numbers deterministically and review confidential details before sharing.
loop.stop: One pass over the selected weekly material and one correction pass; unsupported claims are omitted.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text observations need synthesis across accounts; a dashboard can supply metrics but cannot express the reported context.

steps.what: Discuss buyer reactions, compare tactics and challenge colleagues' interpretations.
Agree a sales experiment, owner and review date.
Copy agreed actions into the team task list.

tasks.design: Existing views in the {CRM} and {BI} assemble the sales evidence pack. A bounded drafting loop combines it with approved notes from the {DOCS}, and a representative reviews the discussion brief before sharing. Colleagues keep the discussion and decisions human, entering agreed experiments directly in the {PROJECT} during the meeting.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful observations are scattered and hard to compare. Capturing context took time, while the value of candid discussion resisted standardisation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured reports reduce preparation work, and bounded summarisation can assemble sourced examples. Direct decision capture removes later copying.
tasks.still_hard: Small samples and selective reporting can make a tactic look effective. Trust, disagreement and tacit buyer knowledge remain central.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge a plausible story, share a failure honestly and help colleagues adapt a tactic to a different buyer.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of one segment-specific sales experiment.

tasks.altitude: The week retains substantial peer discussion but needs less preparation and follow-up copying. With a delegated experiment budget, representatives can test a specific tactic and bring results to the next discussion.

reach.task: Design and evaluate a small sales experiment.
reach.learn: Comparison groups, success measures, sample limitations and stopping criteria.

reach.task: Turn repeated technical objections into a reusable demonstration.
reach.learn: How to separate product limitations from unclear explanations and preserve technical accuracy.

evidence.claim: Configured reports and bounded drafting can reduce preparation while leaving peer discussion and decisions human.
The digest identifies works council consent requirements in the Netherlands for systems that observe employee behaviour or performance.
A structured decision entered during a meeting can remove later task-list transcription.

assumptions: The team already has usable account notes and sales reports.
The discussion brief uses existing authorised records without adding meeting recording.
Agreed experiment fields are entered directly in the {PROJECT} during the decision step.
Experiments remain within existing pricing, claims and outreach authority.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer and employee information; consultation and consent requirements follow national rules.
Build ranges include checking whether the proposed use changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Whether colleagues record enough context for a useful brief.
Who may access account notes across territories.
Whether an employee representative body must be consulted.
What experiment budget and decision authority representatives currently have.
research_questions: Does a short sourced brief improve discussion without suppressing conflicting observations?
Can current reports provide the evidence pack without a new integration?
Which experiment outcomes can be measured without ranking individual sellers?
new_work: Review briefs for missing context, unsupported claims and confidential details.
Maintain access filters and source links.
Review experiment results and retire ineffective tactics.
Check that summaries preserve disagreement rather than presenting false consensus.
tasks.statement: Collaborate with colleagues to exchange information, such as selling strategies or marketing information.

tasks.short: Prepare customer-specific sales presentations and proposals explaining technical products and applications.

steps.what: Clarify the audience, application, buying criteria and proposal scope with relevant stakeholders.
Find approved specifications, application examples, diagrams, commercial terms and relevant estimates.
Adapt the narrative and assemble a presentation or proposal using approved templates.

loop.input: Proposal brief, approved source pack, template sections and permitted claims.
loop.output: Customer-specific narrative with source references, assembled into a proposal draft.
loop.check: Insert specifications, prices and terms deterministically; check narrative claims against sources and render the document for review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unsupported claims are flagged and missing sections return to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout and facts, but explaining an application to different buying audiences needs tailored prose.

steps.what: Review the proposal's technical claims, customer fit, commercial commitments and final wording.
Send the approved proposal or presentation to the agreed customer contacts.
Attach the delivered version and update the opportunity's proposal status.

tasks.design: A generator combines a structured brief from the {CRM} with approved content and templates in the {DOCS}. Deterministic assembly inserts specifications, estimates and terms, while a bounded model drafts the application narrative; approval of the exact version and recipients releases delivery through the {EMAIL} and records it in the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Templates existed, but representatives still searched for current material, tailored the story and copied facts between files. Content ownership and version control limited reliable reuse.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes template assembly, source checks and record updates cheaper to build. A bounded drafting loop can adapt approved material to the customer's application.
tasks.still_hard: The proposal must reflect the real buying decision and avoid unsupported performance claims. Technical diagrams, unusual terms and multilingual layouts still need attention.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the argument that matters to the customer and recognise commitments hidden in seemingly harmless wording.

ambition.what: Provide an application-specific briefing for the customer's operations team alongside the purchasing proposal.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling documents to shaping the technical and commercial case. The representative gains control over audience-specific explanations within approved claims, without gaining authority to change contractual terms.

reach.task: Translate technical specifications into an application explanation for customer stakeholders.
reach.learn: Explain operating limits, evidence for performance claims and the technical implications of exclusions.

reach.task: Review whether a proposal addresses the buying committee's decision criteria.
reach.learn: Stakeholder mapping and concise commercial argument.

evidence.claim: ZARGES reports quote preparation falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds using Elfsquad; this is a vendor case about quotes, not tailored presentations.
Approved content, deterministic document assembly and bounded narrative drafting can support proposal preparation.

assumptions: Approved content can be tagged by product, application, language and validity.
Commercial figures come from approved records rather than generated prose.
The proposal approval includes the exact recipient list, so delivery needs no separate approval interaction.
Preparation includes briefing and review discussions, but excludes delivering a live sales presentation.
Build ranges assume one proposal template and one presentation template initially.
unknowns: Who owns approved claims, diagrams, terms and translations?
Which proposal sections require specialist or commercial approval?
How many templates and languages must the first release support?
Can the {CRM}, {DOCS} and {EMAIL} exchange versioned documents and delivery status?
research_questions: Which document-generation approach best preserves the required editable layouts?
How well can factual checks detect unsupported claims across the required languages?
new_work: Review drafted narrative and document layout.
Retire outdated source material and maintain templates.
Handle missing diagrams, translations and unusual proposal terms.
Check that delivery always uses the approved version and recipients.
tasks.statement: Prepare sales presentations or proposals to explain product specifications or applications.

tasks.short: Help customers resolve technical problems with purchased products.

steps.what: Clarify the symptoms, operating conditions and urgency with the customer.
Find the installed product, relevant manuals, warranty terms and previous support records.
Assess likely causes and decide whether specialist escalation is needed.
Explain approved troubleshooting steps and agree follow-up or specialist involvement.
Record the outcome and assign follow-up to the responsible colleague.

loop.input: Representative's notes, support outcome and follow-up commitment.
loop.output: Draft support record with proposed owner and due date.
loop.check: Representative checks technical statements and commitments; code validates customer, owner and date.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction per case; missing facts return to manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes vary; templates cannot reliably turn them into a useful case summary.

tasks.design: An answer desk joins customer and product identifiers across {CRM}, {ERP}, {HELPDESK} and versioned manuals in {DOCS}. The representative diagnoses and approves advice; a bounded drafting loop prepares the support record, while {WORKFLOW} assigns approved follow-up.
tasks.previous_blocker: Installed-product records and manuals sit apart, and technical advice depends on operating context.
tasks.enabler_now: Search indexes, record links and small drafting loops can be assembled more cheaply with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete installation records, obsolete manuals and safety-critical faults require experienced people.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise misleading symptoms, establish trust and know when the customer should stop operating equipment.

ambition.what: Scheduled post-installation troubleshooting clinics for smaller customer accounts.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence hunting and record entry, leaving room for scheduled troubleshooting clinics. Technical approval rights stay within existing competence limits.

reach.task: Prepare a reproducible fault description for specialist diagnosis.
reach.learn: Operating-condition capture, fault isolation and escalation thresholds.

evidence.claim: Record-backed answers and escalation beyond manuals fit a deterministic answer desk.
Incorrect customer-facing automated answers can create liability; the cited case concerns airline fares, not technical support.
Customer-facing AI interaction requires disclosure under the cited AI Act provision.

assumptions: The representative handles first-line support and escalates specialist cases.
The proposed answer desk is internal; a customer-facing extension needs AI disclosure where applicable.
GDPR applies to customer records. National rules apply to employee monitoring and consultation.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
The conversation remains the largest component despite substantial gains in retrieval and paperwork.
unknowns: Whether installed products have reliable customer and version identifiers.
Which technical advice the representative may approve.
Whether current manuals and support records are accessible through supported interfaces.
Whether national consultation or consent requirements apply to the intended logging.
research_questions: Which recurring questions can be answered directly from approved records?
Which fault categories require immediate specialist escalation?
How often does retrieval select the wrong product revision?
new_work: Review drafted support records and commitments.
Resolve missing product identifiers and stale manual links.
Maintain escalation rules and test retrieval against known faults.
tasks.statement: Provide customers with ongoing technical support.

tasks.short: Explain delivery estimates, service coverage and warranty terms for products customers have purchased.

steps.what: Read the customer's question and identify the relevant purchase.

loop.input: Customer question and supplied purchase reference.
loop.output: Request category and extracted purchase reference, with unresolved fields marked.
loop.check: Validate the category against an allowed list and match the reference to an authorised customer account.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one validation retry; ambiguous identities or categories go to the representative.
loop.why_not_simpler: Email questions use varied wording and may combine delivery, service and warranty requests.

steps.what: Look up purchased items and current delivery estimates.
Check the service contract and warranty version applicable to the purchase.
Resolve unclear coverage or unusual commitments with the service team.
Explain delivery estimates and applicable terms to the customer.
Record the answer and any follow-up commitment.

tasks.design: An answer desk links the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} to approved, versioned terms in the {CLM} and {DOCS}. A bounded loop classifies incoming questions; deterministic lookups and templates prepare answers with source dates and applicable clauses. The representative approves customer messages, handles explanations and records follow-ups through the {CRM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Purchase facts, shipment estimates and historical terms sit in separate places. A current warranty document may not govern an older purchase.
tasks.enabler_now: Record linking, versioned clause libraries and templated answers are established techniques. A small model loop can route varied questions without generating contractual claims.
tasks.still_hard: Historic contracts may lack structured metadata. Coverage disputes, modifications and uncertain delivery estimates still need accountable interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertainty clearly, recognise when the customer needs reassurance and avoid promising coverage or dates beyond authorised terms.

ambition.what: Proactive commissioning-readiness updates for project customers.

tasks.altitude: Routine fact retrieval shrinks, leaving more time for complex service expectations and commissioning risks. The representative gains no automatic right to change warranties, contracts or delivery commitments.

reach.task: Explain installation prerequisites before commissioning.
reach.learn: Product dependencies, safety limits and when a technical specialist must confirm the answer.

reach.task: Keep customer-facing order status accurate.
reach.learn: Shipment milestones, estimate freshness and approved wording for uncertain dates.

evidence.claim: An answer desk can combine structured price, stock, order and warranty records with escalation for unsupported questions.
The digest reports a case where a company was held liable for incorrect information from its chatbot.
Customer-facing AI interaction can require disclosure under Article 50; this matters if direct AI chat is later introduced.

assumptions: Applicable service and warranty versions can be linked to each purchase.
A missing or conflicting term blocks an automatic answer and enters the clarification queue.
Routine answers can use approved templates; complex explanations remain conversations.
Automatic activity records cover messages sent through the workflow; call commitments need human capture.
GDPR access controls prevent disclosure of another customer's orders or contracts.
Build ranges include access review and consultation under national rules if employee monitoring changes.
unknowns: How historic warranty and service versions are stored.
What share of requests requires interpretation rather than factual lookup.
Who may approve exceptional coverage or delivery commitments.
Whether the {CRM} can record sent answers without duplicate activities.
research_questions: Can the existing knowledge and template features support the answer desk?
Can a sample of historic purchases be matched reliably to the correct terms?
Which commissioning prerequisites can be communicated from approved product records?
new_work: Review outgoing answers and handle ambiguous questions.
Maintain approved templates and purchase-to-term mappings.
Remove superseded material from current answer paths while preserving historical versions.
Monitor stale shipment data, failed identity checks and incorrect routing.
tasks.statement: Inform customers of estimated delivery schedules, service contracts, warranties, or other information pertaining to purchased products.

tasks.short: Visit customers to understand technical needs, demonstrate products and agree next actions.

steps.what: Review the account, previous visits, open opportunities and relevant product documents.
Agree the appointment, attendees, agenda and site access arrangements.
Travel to the customer's establishment.
Inspect the application, operating conditions and technical constraints with customer staff.
Discuss needs, demonstrate relevant products and agree possible next actions.
Write the visit report and update requirements and actions in the account.
Send the customer a recap and assign technical follow-up.

tasks.design: A job assembles a linked visit pack from the {CRM}, {ERP} and {DOCS}, while the {CALENDAR} supports appointment coordination. A mobile form in the {CRM} captures observations and agreed actions once; the {WORKFLOW} prepares a checked recap in the {EMAIL} and routes technical questions to the sales engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation and follow-up were scattered across account screens, documents and correspondence. Mobile forms often did not match technical discovery needs.

tasks.statement: Prepare and submit sales contracts for orders.

tasks.short: Contact customers and discuss how technical products could meet their needs.

steps.what: Review account history, open opportunities and previous commitments in the {CRM}.
Choose whom to contact and the purpose of the discussion.
Prepare relevant product material and discovery questions from the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Account facts, contact purpose and approved product material.
loop.output: Short discussion brief with sourced product facts and proposed discovery questions.
loop.check: Require references for claims, label hypotheses and let the representative remove unsuitable questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; insufficient evidence produces questions rather than inferred customer needs.

steps.what: Send a relevant invitation and arrange the discussion through the {EMAIL}.
Discuss needs, constraints and possible product applications with the customer.
Record requirements and follow-up commitments in the {CRM}.

loop.output: Proposed requirement fields, interaction summary and dated follow-up tasks.
loop.check: Trace fields to notes; distinguish customer statements from hypotheses; representative approves commitments.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt; unclear owners or dates remain unset for human completion.

tasks.design: The {CRM} assembles an account brief, and a bounded drafting loop uses the {DOCS} to suggest relevant questions. tasks.previous_blocker: Useful context was spread across activity records and documents. Automated outreach did little to establish whether an approach was relevant or welcome.

tasks.still_hard: Timing, trust and unstated buying constraints remain difficult. Contact eligibility depends on recipient, channel and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Earn permission to explore a problem, notice hesitation and change direction when the customer's priorities differ from the initial hypothesis.

ambition.what: Offer an application discovery session for dormant technical accounts.

Record the preferred configuration, selection rationale and unresolved conditions.

tasks.short: Check materials lists against customer requirements, product records and compatibility rules.

loop.input: Document materials lists; structured lists bypass the model.
loop.output: Item references, quantities, units and revision identifiers with source locations.
loop.check: Validate schema, line counts, quantities, units and exact item matches; review ambiguous or unreadable fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per document; unresolved lines return to manual transcription.
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable document layouts need interpretation; structured imports and fixed templates use deterministic parsing.

steps.what: Compare item codes, quantities, units, revisions and required accessories.
Resolve unclear specifications, substitutions and compatibility exceptions.

tasks.design: Link revision-controlled lists in the {DOCS} to item and configuration records in the {ERP}, then run deterministic completeness and compatibility checks. A bounded extraction loop handles variable document lists; ambiguous fields and technical exceptions go to people. The {WORKFLOW} records the verified revision and passes it to order processing only after required corrections are approved.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer documents vary, revision links are weak and compatibility knowledge is partly undocumented. Manual comparisons bridge documents and product records.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can now be bounded by line-level checks. Faster coding makes item matching, unit validation and revision tracking cheaper to connect.
tasks.still_hard: A valid item code does not prove technical suitability. Missing design context, undocumented dependencies and complex drawings still need engineering review.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising technically plausible but unsuitable combinations and clarifying what the customer actually intends to build.

tasks.short: Verify business customer credit information and route credit exceptions to finance.

Compare rating freshness and customer exposure with credit policy.
